title_en: Shut the Door and Catch the Thief
full_text_zh:
[P1] 关门捉贼

[P2] 唐朝的时候，山东秀才黄巢满腹才华，可他几次到长安城参加科举考试，都没有考中。最后一次落榜时，他挥笔写下一首《不第后赋菊》，然后愤愤地离开了长安城。

不
待到秋来九月八
我花开后百花杀
冲天香阵透长安
满城尽带黄金甲

黄巢

[P3] 黄
黄巢来了！
快跑呀！
谁也没有想到，几年后，黄巢会发动起义，又打回了长安城。这一天，文武百官刚下早朝，
走出皇宫就看见大街上的百姓惊慌地四处乱跑，大叫着："不好了，贼兵打到城外了！"
"贼兵来了，我们该关上城门，出动士兵，守卫皇城呀！"有官员想请示唐僖宗，
可是问遍了皇宫内外，哪儿都找不到皇帝的踪影。

[P4] 原来，一听说贼兵打来了，唐僖宗就慌了手脚，已经在五百名神策军的护卫下，悄悄从金光门逃出了长安城。连皇帝都逃跑了，官员们便也纷纷找地方躲了起来。长安城中的军士和百姓，争先恐后地冲进皇家府库，抢夺里面的金银财宝。

[P5] 就这样，长安城中群龙无首，乱成一团。傍晚的时候，黄巢的先锋军畅通无阻地进了城。长安城的百姓躲在一边，害怕又好奇地观望着。黄巢手下的将领趁机高喊：‘为了百姓，黄王起兵，不征税，不纳粮，不要恐慌！’百姓一听说不用交粮交税，都高高兴兴地出来迎接黄巢了。

[P6] 黄巢坐在贴满黄金的轿子里，
轿子前后的步兵手握亮闪闪的
长矛，骑兵身穿明光铠，连战
马都披着厚重的铠甲。带着浩
浩荡荡的军队，黄巢占领了长
安城。

[P7] 做皇帝可真难！
九天后，长安城中战鼓齐鸣，黄巢登基做了皇帝，国号大齐。做了皇帝后，黄巢却犯了愁，不向百姓收粮收税，国库一点存货都没有呀！将士们分不到钱，就开始抢劫百姓，焚烧店铺和房屋。百姓又吓得东躲西藏起来。

[P8] 再说唐僖宗这边。逃出长安城后，唐僖宗坐着马车，日夜不停地逃跑，随行的宫女和太监脚上都磨出了水泡！他们一路跑到凤翔，凤翔节度使请求唐僖宗留下来，召集兵马，夺回长安。唐僖宗却不肯留下，要再跑远点，跑到更安全的地方。

[P9] 一直逃到千里之外的成都，唐僖宗才放心地停下来。他召集各路大军，从四面八方向长安城围了过去。

"皇上，我愿意带兵退敌！"黄巢手下的将领主动请战。这名将领想："当初我们一仗没打，轻轻松松地拿下了长安城，唐军胆子小得很，吓一吓，他们自己就退兵了！"

[P10] 咚
黄巢命他带着五万兵马，去凤翔攻打唐军。他上了战场，一不整队，二不布阵，只命人擂响战鼓，让士兵们没头没脑地向前乱冲。这一战，黄巢军钻进了唐军的埋伏圈，伤亡两万多人。

[P11] 唐军乘胜追击，一步步逼近了长安城。这时候，是死守长安，还是退出长安？在黄巢的朝堂上，大臣们争得脸红脖子粗。"皇上，长安城外有护城河，城墙又高又厚，还修有瓮城，易守难攻，三五年都攻不破，我们可不能轻易让给唐军呀！"皇上，唐军强悍，兵马又多，不宜硬拼，我们不如以退为进……" 皇上！ 皇上！ 皇上！ 皇上！

[P12] 黄巢军浩浩荡荡地进城来，又垂头丧气地出城去了。百姓一直被黄巢军欺压，看见他们逃走，都跑出家门，一边骂，一边捡起石头、瓦片砸过去。
再三思考后，黄巢下达了命令："军队全部退出长安！"

[P13] 等到三路唐军杀到长安城，他们惊奇地发现：长安城外静悄悄的，没有一个黄巢军把守！
"哈哈，这帮贼兵，跑得还真快。"
唐军欢呼雀跃地进了城。百姓也是欢呼声一片，还捡起黄巢军落下的箭头，送给了唐军。

[P14] 可是，唐军进城放下兵器，第一件事就是冲进百姓的家里，抢走财物绢帛、鸡鸭鱼肉，然后全军上下摆起了庆功宴，一个个喝得东倒西歪，站不起来！

[P15] 晚上，长安城城门大开，唐军既没有派人来关城门，也没有派人把守。当月亮升上天空，城中渐渐安静后，一队队人马从长安城东郊出发，悄悄摸进了城。进城后，他们“嘎吱嘎吱”关上城门，没过多久，城里就火光冲天，哭叫声、喊杀声四起。

[P16] 那些想逃跑的唐军，因为抢劫的财物太多，背着走不动路，四方城门又有黄巢军把守，只好缴械投降了。黄巢就是用这招“关门捉贼”的计策，再一次占据了长安城。

原来，黄巢带兵出城后，就驻扎在长安城东郊等待机会。听探子说完城里的情况，黄巢高兴地说：‘我们可以“关门捉贼”了！’趁唐军呼呼大睡时，黄巢带领军队迅速回到长安城。如神兵天降，黄巢军将毫无戒备的唐军打得抱头乱窜。
full_text_en:
[P1] Trapping the Thief by Closing the Door

[P2] During the Tang Dynasty, Huang Chao, a scholar from Shandong, was full of talent, but he failed the imperial examinations several times after traveling to Chang'an. When he failed for the last time, he wrote a poem titled 'After Failing the Exam, I Write of Chrysanthemums,' then angrily left Chang'an.

Not
Until the ninth month of autumn
When my flowers bloom, all others die
The fragrant array reaches Chang'an
The whole city wears golden armor

Huang Chao

[P3] Huang
Huang Chao is coming!
Run for your lives!
No one could have imagined that, a few years later, Huang Chao would launch a rebellion and return to Chang'an. On this day, after the morning court session, the civil and military officials stepped out of the palace and saw the people on the streets panicking and running in all directions, shouting: "Oh no, the rebel army has reached the city gates!"
"The rebels are here! We must close the city gates, mobilize the soldiers, and defend the imperial city!" an official tried to report to Emperor Xizong,
but after searching the entire palace, they could not find the emperor anywhere.

[P4] Originally, upon hearing that the rebel troops had arrived, Emperor Xizong of Tang panicked and, under the protection of five hundred Shence Army soldiers, secretly fled Chang'an City through the Jinguang Gate. With the emperor gone, officials hurriedly scattered and hid. Soldiers and civilians in Chang'an rushed into the imperial treasury, scrambling to seize its gold and treasures.

[P5] Thus, Chang'an City was in chaos, leaderless and in disarray. In the evening, Huang Chao's vanguard troops entered the city without resistance. The people of Chang'an hid on the side, frightened yet curiously watching. A general under Huang Chao seized the opportunity to shout: 'For the people, King Huang has risen in rebellion! No taxes, no grain tribute, no need to panic!' Upon hearing they wouldn't have to pay grain or taxes, the people happily came out to welcome Huang Chao.

[P6] Huang Chao sat in a palanquin covered in gold,
with infantrymen in front and behind holding shiny spears,
cavalrymen wearing bright armor,
even the warhorses draped in heavy armor.
With a vast and mighty army, Huang Chao took control of Chang'an City.

[P7] Being emperor is really hard!
Nine days later, war drums echoed through Chang'an as Huang Chao ascended the throne, establishing the state of Da Qi. After becoming emperor, Huang Chao was troubled: without collecting grain or taxes from the people, the state treasury had no reserves at all! Since the soldiers received no money, they began robbing the people and burning shops and houses. The common folk, frightened, fled in all directions to hide.

[P8] Now, let's talk about Emperor Xizong. After fleeing from Chang'an, Emperor Xizong rode in a carriage, running day and night. The palace ladies and eunuchs accompanying him had blisters on their feet! They ran all the way to Fengxiang, where the local military governor begged Emperor Xizong to stay, gather troops, and retake Chang'an. But Emperor Xizong refused to stay, insisting on running even farther to a safer place.

[P9] After fleeing all the way to Chengdu, thousands of miles away, Emperor Xizong finally stopped and felt safe. He gathered troops from all directions and surrounded Chang'an City.

"Your Majesty, I am willing to lead the troops to repel the enemy!" A general under Huang Chao volunteered for battle. The general thought: "At first, we took Chang'an City without fighting a single battle. The Tang army is very cowardly; just scare them a bit, and they will retreat on their own!"

[P10] Dong
Huang Chao ordered him to lead 50,000 troops to attack the Tang army in Fengxiang. Once on the battlefield, he neither formed ranks nor arranged formations, but only ordered the war drums to be beaten, causing the soldiers to charge forward wildly without direction. In this battle, Huang Chao's army fell into the Tang army's ambush, suffering over 20,000 casualties.

[P11] The Tang army pressed forward, gradually approaching Chang'an. At this moment, should they hold out in Chang'an or retreat? In Huang Chao's court, ministers argued fiercely. "Your Majesty, outside Chang'an there is a moat, the city walls are high and thick, with a barbican, easy to defend and hard to attack—three or five years and they still couldn't break through! We must not easily surrender to the Tang army!" "Your Majesty, the Tang army is powerful, with many troops and horses. It's not wise to fight head-on. We should retreat to advance..." "Your Majesty! Your Majesty! Your Majesty! Your Majesty!"

[P12] The Huang Chao army marched into the city in great numbers, but then left in low spirits. The people, who had long been oppressed by Huang Chao's troops, rushed out of their homes upon seeing them flee, shouting insults and throwing stones and tiles at them.
After much deliberation, Huang Chao issued the order: "All troops, withdraw from Chang'an!"

[P13] When the three armies of the Tang Dynasty arrived at Chang'an, they were surprised to find: the area outside the city was quiet, with not a single Huang Chao soldier guarding it!
"Haha, these bandits ran away really fast."
The Tang army joyfully entered the city. The people also cheered, and even picked up the arrows left behind by Huang Chao's army, giving them to the Tang soldiers.

[P14] But as soon as the Tang army entered the city and put down their weapons, the first thing they did was rush into the homes of the common people, stealing silk, cloth, chickens, ducks, and fish. Then, the entire army threw a victory banquet, getting so drunk they staggered and couldn't stand up!

[P15] At night, the gates of Chang'an were wide open, and the Tang army had neither sent anyone to close the gates nor posted guards. When the moon rose into the sky and the city gradually grew quiet, squad after squad of troops set out from the eastern suburbs of Chang'an and stealthily entered the city. After entering, they "creeeak creeeak" shut the gates. Not long after, the city was ablaze with fire, and cries of sorrow and shouts of battle erupted everywhere.

[P16] Those Tang soldiers who wanted to flee, having looted too much treasure, could not walk with the heavy load. With all four city gates guarded by Huang Chao's troops, they had no choice but to surrender. Huang Chao used this 'trapping the thief by closing the gate' strategy to once again seize control of Chang'an.

Originally, after Huang Chao led his troops out of the city, he stationed them in the eastern suburbs of Chang'an, waiting for the right moment. Upon hearing the scout's report about the situation inside the city, Huang Chao happily said, 'We can now “trap the thief by closing the gate”!' Seizing the moment when the Tang soldiers were sound asleep, Huang Chao swiftly led his army back into Chang'an. Like divine soldiers descending from heaven, Huang Chao's forces routed the completely unprepared Tang troops, who scrambled in panic.
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本标题页，标题为“关门捉贼”，画面中央是一位身穿黄色古装、面带笑容的胖男子，双臂交叉于胸前，表情自信。
[P2] 本页讲述了唐朝山东秀才黄巢屡试不第，最后一次落榜后愤然离开长安城，并写下《不第后赋菊》一诗的情景。画面左侧为黄巢在雨中题诗，右侧为他愤怒离去的背影。
[P3] 黄巢率军攻入长安城，百姓惊慌逃窜，官员们发现皇帝已不见踪影，城内陷入混乱。
[P4] 本页描绘了唐僖宗在贼兵来袭时惊慌失措，率五百神策军从金光门逃出长安城，官员和百姓纷纷逃窜或哄抢府库财宝的混乱场面。
[P5] 黄巢的先锋军顺利攻入长安城，城中混乱无主。黄巢部将向百姓宣告不征税、不纳粮，百姓听后纷纷高兴地出来迎接黄巢。
[P6] 黄巢率军攻入长安城，他乘坐贴满黄金的轿子，士兵和战马皆披重甲，浩浩荡荡地占领了长安。
[P7] 黄巢登基称帝后，因国库空虚、无法支付军饷，导致士兵抢劫百姓、焚烧房屋，百姓惊恐逃散，黄巢感叹‘做皇帝可真难！’
[P8] 本页描绘了唐僖宗在逃出长安后，继续向凤翔方向逃亡，随行人员疲惫不堪，凤翔节度使请求其留下组织反击，但唐僖宗执意继续逃往更远的安全地带。
[P9] 唐僖宗逃到成都后召集大军围攻长安，黄巢部下将领主动请战，认为唐军胆小，只需吓唬即可退兵。
[P10] 本页描绘了黄巢派兵攻打凤翔，因指挥混乱、不设阵型，导致军队陷入唐军埋伏，伤亡惨重的战斗场面。
[P11] 唐军逼近长安，黄巢朝堂上大臣们就是否死守长安展开激烈争论，有人主张坚守，有人建议以退为进，场面混乱。
[P12] 黄巢军队攻入长安后因战况不利而撤退，百姓趁机追击并投掷石块瓦片；黄巢在深思后下令全军退出长安。
[P13] 三路唐军抵达长安城外，发现黄巢军队已撤退，城外空无一人。唐军进城后，百姓欢呼庆祝，捡起黄巢军遗留的箭头赠予唐军。
[P14] 唐军攻入长安后，未顾百姓安危，立即抢夺财物、大摆宴席，士兵们醉酒后东倒西歪，行为失当。
[P15] 唐军趁夜潜入长安城，关闭城门后纵火劫掠，城中火光冲天，百姓哭喊声四起。
[P16] 本页讲述了黄巢利用‘关门捉贼’之计，趁唐军劫掠后疲惫不堪、戒备松懈之际，率军突袭并重新占领长安城的过程。
